ratings.concept: Modes of vegetative and asexual reproduction tied to named organisms: rhizome in banana, conidia in Penicillium, offset in water hyacinth, fragmentation rather than binary fission in Sargassum
ratings.reason: This question requires four separate stored structure-to-organism associations judged under a negated task, demonstrated by the stem's 'Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?' standing over four single pairs, 'Rhizome - Banana', 'Binary fission - Sargassum', 'Conidia - Penicillium' and 'Offset - Water hyacinth'.
ratings.note: The key as stored is option 4, 'Offset - Water hyacinth'. That pairing is the standard one: Eichhornia spreads by offsets. Option 2, 'Binary fission - Sargassum', is the pairing that does not hold, since Sargassum is a brown alga that multiplies by fragmentation while binary fission is the protistan mode. I do not overturn the key (rulebook section 7): the question is tagged as printed and arguable_key records the doubt, the repair being a check of this item against the printed paper and of our stored correct_answer. Two consequences follow for the axes. No trap is written: siting a trap requires naming an option that is not the answer, and the only option here with a nameable device is the one the subject matter indicates is the answer, so any trap would be a trap on the answer. No elimination either: the one available shortcut - the three secure pairings strike out options 1, 3 and 4 - lands on option 2 and so contradicts the stored key, which is the doubt itself rather than a strategy the question offers. has_figure is true with figure_image at figures_agent/2015_A/q134.png; all four options are complete as text and need no figure.
